messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: ALB health churn detected in eastus-azb -> high 5xx rate on /api/v1/infer (5m avg 18%). Auto-escalating to #incidents.

emma.chen: seeing 502/504s from our edge -> customers reporting partial responses. Any impact to dedicated customers?

raj.patel: yep a couple of dedicated pools show >10% request errors, not all regions. Cross-region routing looks weird, some traffic mirrored to eu-west while origin is eastus.

jules_sre: grabbing logs now. running: `kubectl -n ingress logs deploy/ingress-controller --since=5m | grep error | tail -n 50`

matt_connors: i'm on infra. ALB targetgroup states flapping - targets toggling Unhealthy -> Healthy repeatedly. Possible NLB healthprobe timeouts upstream?

kavya_support: customers: two enterprise tenants reported increased latency and aborted responses (support ticket #3421 and #3422). Noticed spike started ~1767009600.

emma.chen: ok immediate mitigation ideas: 1) increase ALB deregistration delay to avoid churn 2) temporarily route traffic away from azb to azc where healthy 3) bump envoy retry and timeout to mask transient errors

raj.patel: i can do a canary route to azc. changing weighted routing in our traffic router to 80/20 azb/azc -> 20/80 azb/azc? want to move 70% -> 30% to azc. will publish with short TTL.

jules_sre: hold on, before routing change let's increase healthcheck threshold so transient failures don't flip states. run: `aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn $TG_INGRESS_AZB --health-check-interval-seconds 10 --healthy-threshold-count 4 --unhealthy-threshold-count 6`

matt_connors: i applied a conservative change to deregistration delay (set to 120s) and bumped unhealthy threshold to 6. watching metrics.

incident-bot: Pager: paging oncall: raj.patel (primary), jules_sre (secondary) -> ack required

raj.patel: ack. i'll take lead.

jules_sre: ack. standing by for logs correlation and cluster-level telemetry.

emma.chen: raj can you also check control-plane EBS/NIC errors? last week similar signature was caused by a noisy host in azb.

raj.patel: already running `aws ec2 describe-instance-status --filters Name=availability-zone,Values=us-east-2b` to spot instance-level warnings. nothing obvious yet. getting container-level CPU and socket resets in envoy. excerpt: 
```
[2026-04-12T12:14:03Z] envoy[x.y.z]: connection reset by peer while proxying to upstream 10.44.2.9:8080
[2026-04-12T12:14:07Z] healthcheck failed for target i-0abc12345 status=504
```

matt_connors: i'm seeing increased SYN-RSTs at the LB to instance layer. filing ticket with cloud provider in parallel.

kavya_support: public status page updated: "Partial degraded responses for inference API in US-East region. Engineers investigating. Updates every 15m." customers notified.

emma.chen: action plan (short):
- (raj) shift 60% traffic to azc within 10m, monitor errors per-customer
- (jules) correlate envoy retries & pod restarts, raise alert if pod restarts >3 in 5m
- (matt) open cloud support case and request targetgroup debugging; also check host NIC errors and host-level metrics
- (kavya) keep support tickets and status page updated

raj.patel: starting weighted routing shift now. command: `./routerctl set-weight ingress eastus azb=30 azc=70 --dry-run=false --ttl=30`

incident-bot: ACTION: route_change executed by raj.patel at 1767009979 -> azb 30% / azc 70% TTL 30s

jules_sre: after route change 2m: 5xx rate dropped from 18% -> 5% in azc, azb still at 12%. pod crashloop not observed but envoy socket resets persist on a few hosts. collecting pcap for one host.

matt_connors: cloud support responded: seeing an unusual number of failed healthchecks from our targets linked to transient kernel-level network stack issues on 3 hosts in azb. They recommended draining and replacing hosts.

emma.chen: good. Do we want full AZ failover or targeted host replacement? full AZ failover will impact capacity and may push load to other regions.

raj.patel: prefer targeted host replacement + scaled up capacity in azc for headroom. i'll launch replacement for the 3 suspect instances and cordon/evict pods gracefully: `kubectl drain node/<node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60` then terminate instance.

jules_sre: creating a temporary Envoy retry policy to reduce user-surface errors: update config to retries: 3, per_try_timeout: 2s for /api/v1/infer. deploying via our rollout job.

incident-bot: NOTE: rollout job triggered by jules_sre at 1767010142 -> rollout/ingress-envoy-retry-v2

kavya_support: customer update posted at 12:25 UTC: "Mitigation in progress: routing shifted; host replacements underway. We will provide another update in 30 minutes."

matt_connors: replaced 3 instances in azb, after replacement healthchecks stabilized. network kernel counters zeroed on new hosts.

raj.patel: traffic steering back to 60/40 azb/azc gradually. `./routerctl set-weight ingress eastus azb=60 azc=40 --ttl=60`

jules_sre: monitoring shows 5xx at region-level down to baseline (~1%). no ongoing spikes for 15m. envoy resets gone for replaced hosts.

emma.chen: excellent. summary for postmortem notes: root cause likely host-level kernel network stack flapping in azb causing healthcheck churn -> ALB target flaps -> ingress showing 5xx. Contributing factor: low deregistration/unhealthy thresholds allowed fast churn. Mitigations: increased thresholds, replaced hosts, temporary routing, envoy retry policy.

kavya_support: support: closing duplicate tickets and notifying impacted customers of resolution. will re-open if anything crops up.

raj.patel: moving incident to postmortem stage. assigning owners: RCA lead = jules_sre, infra followup = matt_connors, deployment policy followup = emma.chen.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> moving to monitoring. incident status: resolved (impact reduced to baseline). Logs, actions and owners recorded in incident runbook: https://internal.redwood/incident/1767009876

emma.chen: thanks everyone — great coordination.

kavya_support: final status update posted at 12:47 UTC: "Resolved: services returned to normal after targeted host replacements and routing changes. Postmortem forthcoming."

jules_sre: adding note: follow-up items - increase default ALB health thresholds for ingress targetgroups; create playbook for targeted host drain/replace in AZ; tighten monitoring for envoy socket resets.

raj.patel: closing thread unless new alerts.
